items.question: Following a single engine failure, what power level is automatically available to the operating engine without further pilot switch action?
options: 30 second power
2 minute power
Maximum continuous power
OEI continuous power
items.explanation: After a single engine failure, the operative engine automatically has 30 second power available. The pilot can then select 2 minute power by moving the collective OEI SEL switch aft, and maximum continuous power by first selecting 2 minute power and then pushing in on the OEI SEL switch.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.4 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-5)

items.question: Which indication distinguishes an actual single engine failure from an ENGINE FIXED POWER (FADEC) malfunction?
options: An actual engine failure shows a red X over the engine pod on EICAS together with an ENGINE FAILURE aural alert, which a FADEC fixed-power malfunction does not produce
Both conditions produce an identical red X and aural alert
A FADEC malfunction always shows Ng below 50%, identical to an engine failure
An actual engine failure never triggers an aural alert
items.explanation: An engine failure is always accompanied by a #1/#2 ENG OUT warning light, an ENGINE FAILURE aural alert, and a red X over the failed engine pod on EICAS. An engine with a FADEC-caused fixed power malfunction shows none of these and retains Ng above 50% airborne (above 63% on the ground).
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.4 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE / 3.4 ENGINE FIXED POWER (p.3-5, p.3-14A)

items.question: How does the pilot select two-minute OEI power after a single engine failure?
options: Move the collective OEI SEL switch aft
Push in on the OEI SEL switch
Push forward on the OEI SEL switch
Cycle the affected throttle from FLY to IDLE and back
items.explanation: Moving the collective OEI SEL switch aft selects 2 minute power. Pushing in on the switch (after 2 minute power is already selected) gives maximum continuous power, and pushing forward re-arms 30 second power.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.4 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-5)

items.question: What is the immediate, critical pilot action upon a dual engine failure?
options: Immediately reduce collective and enter autorotation
Attempt an air restart of both engines before touching the collective
Increase collective to cushion the aircraft
Apply the rotor brake
items.explanation: Nr will decay rapidly to an unrecoverable state with resultant loss of aircraft control unless autorotation is entered immediately after a dual engine failure; immediate collective reduction is required to maintain Nr within safe limits.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 2.0 DUAL-ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-10B)

items.question: A FADEC Channel A failure specifically causes loss of which indications on the affected engine?
options: Engine oil temperature and TGT indications, with ENG POWER LIM illuminated
Engine oil pressure and TGT indications, with ENG POWER LIM illuminated
Complete loss of both engines
Loss of collective authority on both engines
items.explanation: A Channel A failure causes loss of the affected engine's oil temperature and TGT indications, and disables ENG OIL HOT, FUEL BYPASS and ENG OIL PRES cautions, with ENG POWER LIM illuminated. A Channel B failure instead causes loss of oil pressure and TGT indications.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.2 FADEC CHANNEL FAILURE (p.3-13)

items.question: What indicates an ENGINE FIXED POWER ("fail fixed") condition?
options: A torque split, with the affected engine not responding to collective movements
A complete loss of torque on the affected engine
Ng above 108.5% on the affected engine
Illumination of the FIRE/ARMED pushbutton
items.explanation: ENG 1/2 FIXED PWR is indicated by a torque split where the affected engine does not respond to collective movements, because loss of both Np signals and the Nr signal to a FADEC freezes that engine's power at the setting it had when the sensors failed.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.4 ENGINE FIXED POWER (p.3-14/3-14A)

items.question: What Np or Ng values define an engine overspeed condition that causes the FADEC to shut off fuel to the affected engine?
options: Np above 120% or Ng above 108.5%
Np above 106% or Ng above 100%
Np above 100% or Ng above 95%
Np above 141% or Ng above 120%
items.explanation: Np above 120% or Ng above 108.5% are overspeed conditions that cause the FADEC to shut off fuel to the affected engine; the FADEC automatically restarts the engine once Ng and Np return within limits.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.8 ENGINE OVERSPEED (p.3-17)

items.question: What action is required immediately after an ENG CHIP caution illuminates?
options: No action is required until a safe single engine airspeed is attained; then reduce the affected engine to idle and land as soon as practical
Perform an immediate emergency engine shutdown
Continue the flight with no change to engine handling
Shut down the unaffected engine to preserve the affected one
items.explanation: An ENG CHIP caution indicates metal particles in the affected oil system; no action is required until a safe single engine airspeed is obtained, after which the affected throttle is reduced to idle and the flight is landed as soon as practical.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 4.3 ENGINE CHIP INDICATION (p.3-22)

items.question: What main fuel quantity confirms a FUEL LOW caution?
options: Less than 215 ± 45 pounds
Less than 500 pounds
Less than 100 pounds
Less than 1,000 pounds
items.explanation: A FUEL LOW caution is confirmed by main fuel quantity less than 215 ± 45 pounds, along with the fuel level turning yellow on the EICAS page.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 5.1 FUEL LOW (p.3-25)

items.question: During a crossfeed-position start of the second engine, why might PRIME PUMP FAIL illuminate without an actual pump failure?
options: The already-running engine's mechanical fuel pump overpowers the prime pump, causing a low pressure reading at the prime pump sensor
The prime pump always fails during the second engine start
The crossfeed valve is mechanically stuck closed
The FADEC intentionally disables the prime pump during crossfeed starts
items.explanation: When starting the second engine with fuel valves in crossfeed, the operating engine's mechanical fuel pump can overpower the prime pump, causing a low pressure reading at the prime pump sensor — this is not an actual prime pump failure, which is instead confirmed if the caution remains illuminated after the starter cuts out.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 5.2 PRIME PUMP FAIL (p.3-25/3-26)

items.question: After an automatic APU shutdown (APU FAIL caution), what must the pilot NOT do?
options: Attempt to restart the APU
Set AIR SRCE HEAT/START to ENG
Continue the flight
Monitor TGT on the pilot inboard EICAS display
items.explanation: After an automatic APU shutdown, the pilot must not attempt to restart the APU. The APU generator will not be available for emergency power or engine shutdown, so TGT should be monitored and external power connected if available.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 6.1 APU FAILURE (p.3-27)

items.question: What does the APU OVERLOAD caution indicate, and what is the first action?
options: APU generator load is in excess of normal limits; decrease APU electrical load by turning off nonessential systems
APU oil pressure is low; shut down the APU immediately
The APU EGT thermocouple has failed; land immediately
The APU generator has completely failed; switch to battery power only
items.explanation: APU OVERLOAD indicates the APU generator load exceeds normal limits. The first action is to decrease APU electrical load by turning off nonessential systems; if the caution remains, attain VMC and land as soon as practical.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 6.5 APU OVERLOAD (p.3-29)

items.question: At what MGB oil pressure does the RFM require the pilot to Land Immediately?
options: Below 5 psi
Below 35 psi
Below 45 psi
Below 24 psi
items.explanation: A total loss of MGB oil pressure below 5 psi may result in MGB failure in less than 10 minutes, requiring the pilot to Land Immediately. The MGB OIL PRES caution/warning thresholds (45 psi / 35 psi at the manifold) trigger the initial caution/warning but not the Land Immediately requirement by themselves.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 7.1 MAIN GEARBOX OIL PRESSURE WARNING (p.3-31/3-32)

items.question: Within how many seconds must MGB OIL BYP be selected after the MGB OIL PRES warning illuminates?
options: 5 seconds
30 seconds
60 seconds
10 minutes
items.explanation: BYP must be selected within 5 seconds after the MGB OIL PRES warning illuminates, to ensure an adequate quantity of oil remains in the gearbox.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 7.1 MAIN GEARBOX OIL PRESSURE WARNING (p.3-32)

items.question: What is the result of a dual AC generator failure (AC GEN 1 FAIL and AC GEN 2 FAIL)?
options: Loss of all electrical systems except those powered by the battery buses, including loss of copilot displays
No operational impact provided the APU generator is already running
Immediate loss of hydraulic boost pressure only
Automatic shutdown of both engines
items.explanation: A dual AC generator failure results in loss of all electrical systems except those powered by the battery buses, including loss of copilot displays, until the APU generator or the AC generators are recovered.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 8.2 DUAL AC GENERATOR FAILURE (p.3-35)

items.question: After a dual DC converter and backup converter failure with the converters not recovered, why must the landing gear be lowered before battery power is depleted?
options: Normal and emergency extension of the landing gear is not possible without electrical power
The landing gear free-falls automatically once battery power is exhausted
Electrical power has no relationship to landing gear operation
The emergency blow-down system requires AC generator power specifically
items.explanation: Normal and emergency extension of the landing gear is not possible without electrical power, so when operating on battery power only, the landing gear should be lowered before battery power is depleted.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 8.6 DUAL DC CONVERTER and BACKUP CONVERTER FAILURE (p.3-39)

items.question: With both primary hydraulic pumps failed (HYD 1 PUMP FAIL and HYD 2 PUMP FAIL), what maintains control of the aircraft?
options: The #3 hydraulic system pressurizes the primary servos
The AFCS SAS system fully replaces hydraulic assistance
Manual reversion of the flight controls with no hydraulic assistance
The APU hydraulic pump automatically engages
items.explanation: With loss of both primary hydraulic systems, the #3 hydraulic system pressurizes the primary servos, allowing continued control of the aircraft while control inputs are restricted to moderate rates.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 9.1 DUAL HYDRAULIC PUMP FAILURE (p.3-42)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for activating the landing gear emergency blow down (EMER DN) system?
options: 90 KIAS
120 KIAS
60 KIAS
150 KIAS
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for activation of the landing gear emergency blow down switch is 90 KIAS, consistent with the airspeed limit stated in the Operating Limitations section.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 10.1 LANDING GEAR WILL NOT EXTEND (p.3-48/3-49)

items.question: What is the correct response to a loss of tail rotor thrust in forward flight (sharp, uncommanded right yaw unresponsive to pedal inputs)?
options: Enter autorotation immediately and maintain 80 to 100 KIAS
Increase collective to arrest the yaw and maintain level flight
Reduce airspeed to a hover and land vertically without entering autorotation
Apply full left pedal and continue powered flight
items.explanation: Loss of tail rotor thrust in forward flight is a loss-of-drive failure that makes level flight impossible; the pilot must enter autorotation immediately and maintain 80 to 100 KIAS to touchdown.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 11.1 LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT (p.3-51)

items.question: In flight, after confirming an engine fire, what is the correct order of the initial actions?
options: Adjust collective to single engine power, stop the affected throttle, then push in FIRE/ARMED and deploy the fire extinguisher
Push in FIRE/ARMED immediately without first adjusting collective or the throttle
Land immediately without first securing the affected engine
Shut down both engines simultaneously
items.explanation: After confirming an in-flight engine fire, the pilot adjusts collective to single engine power, stops the affected throttle, pushes in the FIRE/ARMED pushbutton, and deploys MAIN/RESERVE fire extinguisher as required, before accomplishing the SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE procedure and landing.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 13.1 ENGINE FIRES (p.3-60)

items.question: In the S-92 Emergency Procedures, what does the term "land as soon as possible" mean?
options: Continued flight may not be possible; ditching or landing in hazardous terrain is preferable to continuing flight
Land at the nearest site where a safe landing can be accomplished
Extended flight is not recommended; landing site and duration of flight are at the pilot's discretion
Land at the nearest airfield where maintenance support is available
items.explanation: The RFM defines "land as soon as possible" as landing at the nearest site where a safe landing can be accomplished. "Land immediately" means continued flight may not be possible and ditching or landing in hazardous terrain is preferable to continuing flight; "land as soon as practical" means extended flight is not recommended, with landing site and duration of flight at the pilot's discretion.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: INTRODUCTION (p.3-2)

items.question: According to the Emergency Procedures introduction, when should the pilot reset a popped circuit breaker?
options: Up to three times, provided the associated caution extinguishes each time
At any time, as long as the associated system caution is illuminated
Only if the affected system is required for flight, only once, and only if there is no indication of electrical fire
Only on the ground, after the electrical system has been checked
items.explanation: A circuit breaker should be reset only if the affected system is required for flight. The pilot should reset a circuit breaker only once and only if there is no indication of electrical fire.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: INTRODUCTION (p.3-2)

items.question: After an emergency engine shutdown (throttle STOP, FUEL OFF), TGT remains above 540°. What does the procedure call for?
options: Press the ENG START button to engage the starter with the throttle in STOP, and press it again to turn the starter off when TGT is below 150°
Push in the FIRE/ARMED pushbutton and discharge the main fire extinguisher bottle
Move the throttle to IDLE to restore airflow until TGT is below 540°
Wait until TGT is below 150°, then select FUEL back to DIRECT
items.explanation: If TGT remains above 540° or there is other evidence of combustion after engine shutdown, press the ENG START button to engage the starter with the throttle in STOP. When TGT is below 150°, press the ENG START button to turn the starter off.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.1 EMERGENCY ENGINE SHUTDOWN (p.3-3)

items.question: An engine flamed out while its fuel selector was in XFD. According to ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT, what should be done with the fuel selector for the restart?
options: Leave it in XFD so the operating engine's fuel supply primes the failed engine
Select OFF until Ng passes ground idle, then return it to XFD
Place the fuel selector switch to DIRECT during the restart sequence
Place it to OFF and restart only with APU bleed air
items.explanation: The ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT procedure assumes the engine was operating with the fuel selector in DIRECT. If the flameout occurred while operating in XFD, place the fuel selector switch to DIRECT during the restart sequence.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.2 ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT (p.3-3)

items.question: During an in-flight engine restart using crossbleed air, what does the CAUTION require on the operating engine?
options: At least 80% torque
At least 95% Ng
At least 100% Nr with 30 second power armed
At least 90% Ng
items.explanation: The CAUTION states: maintain at least 90% Ng on the operating engine when accomplishing a crossbleed start. The same caution appears in both ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT and EMERGENCY ENGINE START.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.2 ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT / 1.3 EMERGENCY ENGINE START (p.3-4, p.3-5)

items.question: During an in-flight engine restart with AIR SRCE HEAT/START in ENG and the APU on, which air source does the system use?
options: The operating engine if it is at approximately 80% torque or above; otherwise the APU
Always the APU, since the APU has priority whenever it is running
Always the operating engine, since ENG is selected
The operating engine if it is below approximately 80% torque; otherwise the APU
items.explanation: With the AIR SRCE HEAT/START switch in ENG and the APU on, the system uses the engine as the air source if the operating engine is at approximately 80% torque or above; below approximately 80% torque it uses the APU. The APU should be ON for in-flight restarts if possible, and use of engine cross-bleed results in a loss of up to 3% power of the operating engine.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.2 ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT (p.3-4)

items.question: What protection is absent during the EMERGENCY ENGINE START procedure, and what must the pilot do about it?
options: None; FADEC hot start prevention remains active, so no pilot intervention is required
FADEC hot start prevention is not present; the pilot must monitor engine temperature and place the throttle to STOP if a hot start is imminent
Hot start prevention remains active, but the pilot must hold the throttle in IDLE until TGT is below 540°C
FADEC hot start prevention is not present; the pilot should move the throttle to IDLE if a hot start is imminent
items.explanation: During normal engine starts, hot start prevention is provided automatically by the FADEC. This protective feature is not present during an emergency start procedure: the pilot must monitor engine temperature and manually abort the start by placing the throttle to STOP if a hot start is imminent. An emergency start is only to be used when damage to the engine is secondary to safety of flight.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.3 EMERGENCY ENGINE START (p.3-4, p.3-5)

items.question: During the EMERGENCY ENGINE START procedure, when is the throttle of the affected engine moved to FLY?
options: Only once Ng has stabilized at ground idle
When TGT is below 540°C, and never sooner
Only after the FADEC automatic blow down has completed
When TGT is below 150°C, or sooner if the situation dictates
items.explanation: The emergency start sequence is: APU CTRL ON (if time permits), AIR SRCE HEAT/START to ENG (if APU is OFF) or APU (if APU is ON), ENG IGN AUTO, FUEL selector DIRECT or XFD, throttle OFF, ENG START button PRESS, then throttle to FLY when TGT is below 150°C or sooner if the situation dictates. The emergency start procedure overrides the FADEC automatic blow down.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.3 EMERGENCY ENGINE START (p.3-4, p.3-5)

items.question: After a single engine failure, how is 30 second power re-armed?
options: By moving the collective OEI SEL switch aft
By pushing in on the collective OEI SEL switch
By pushing forward on the collective OEI SEL switch, at any time
By cycling the operating engine throttle from FLY to IDLE and back
items.explanation: Thirty second power can be re-armed at any time by pushing forward on the OEI SEL switch. After an engine failure, 30 second power is attained by raising the collective until Nr decreases to 100%. Moving the switch aft selects two minute power; pushing in on it (after two minute power is selected) selects maximum continuous power.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.4 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-6)

items.question: While cushioning a single engine landing, Nr droops below 96%. If the APU and APU generator are not on, what is the result?
options: The AFCS disengages and aircraft control is degraded until Nr recovers
The AC generators drop off line, only the battery bus powers aircraft systems and the copilot MFDs momentarily blank, with no degradation to aircraft control
The pilot MFDs blank and remain blank until the generators are reset manually
The operating engine automatically selects two minute power to restore Nr
items.explanation: When increasing collective to cushion a single engine landing, Nr may droop below 96%, causing the AC generators to drop off line at touchdown. Unless the APU is on and the APU generator switch is on, only the battery bus will be available. This does not degrade aircraft control but causes the copilot MFDs to momentarily blank. Once the collective is moved to flat pitch and Nr recovers above 96%, normal electrical power returns.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.4 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-6)

items.question: Extended single engine flight is needed to reach a safe landing area. When does the RFM say NOT to use fuel crossfeed?
options: When the pilot suspects the engine failed due to a fuel system malfunction
When fuel imbalance exceeds 700 pounds (317 kg)
Whenever the APU is running
At any time during single engine flight
items.explanation: If extended single engine flight is required, the pilot should use the fuel crossfeed system to prevent exceeding 700 pounds (317 kg) of fuel imbalance or to prevent flaming out the good engine due to fuel starvation. Do not crossfeed if the pilot suspects that the engine failed due to a fuel system malfunction.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.4 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-6)

items.question: An engine fails during a Category A horizontal takeoff exactly at the takeoff decision point (TDP). What does the RFM direct?
options: Continue the takeoff, since the TDP has been reached
Continue the takeoff only if Vtoss has already been reached
Reject the takeoff
Either option, at the pilot's discretion, depending on remaining distance
items.explanation: If the engine fails before or at the takeoff decision point (TDP), the takeoff is rejected. If the failure occurs after the TDP, the takeoff may be continued. Prior to reaching TDP, the rejected takeoff is initiated by rotating nose up to decrease forward speed and attain a landing attitude.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.6 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — CATEGORY "A" HORIZONTAL (p.3-6, p.3-6A)

items.question: Following an engine failure on a Category A takeoff, what rotor speed does the RFM specify from the TDP up to the best rate of climb speed, and for single engine flight above it?
options: 105% Nr up to Vy, then 100% Nr above Vy
104% Nr throughout the climb and in single engine cruise
100% Nr throughout, including single engine flight above Vy
100% Nr from TDP to Vy (80 KIAS), then 105% Nr for single engine flight above Vy
items.explanation: During a Category A climbout, 100% Nr is used to maximize climb rates from TDP to the best rate of climb speed of 80 KIAS. For single engine flight above the best rate of climb airspeed, use 105% Nr.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.6 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — CATEGORY "A" HORIZONTAL (p.3-6)

items.question: After an engine failure past the TDP in a Category A horizontal takeoff, when should two minute power be selected?
options: Immediately at the engine failure, before adjusting pitch attitude
Not until obstacle clearance is assured; select it when obstacles are cleared
On reaching Vtoss, before retracting the landing gear
Only after reaching Vy and selecting maximum continuous power
items.explanation: After TDP: adjust pitch attitude to establish Vtoss, adjust collective to maintain 100% Nr, and retract the landing gear when a positive rate of climb is established. A WARNING states: do not select two minute power until obstacle clearance is assured. When obstacles are cleared, select two minute power, continue the climb and accelerate to Vy, then select maximum continuous power and land as soon as practical.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.6 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — CATEGORY "A" HORIZONTAL (p.3-7)

items.question: An engine fails in a hover at 5 to 15 feet. What is the first action in the RFM procedure?
options: Lower the collective immediately to preserve Nr
Maintain the collective setting
Select two minute power and climb out
Rotate nose down to gain airspeed
items.explanation: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE — HOVER (5-15 FEET): 1. Collective — maintain collective setting. 2. Increase collective to cushion landing. 3. After touchdown, neutralize cyclic and reduce collective to minimum. 4. Apply wheel brakes.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.5 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE — HOVER (5-15 FEET) (p.3-6)

items.question: An engine fails before the TDP during a ground level helipad vertical takeoff. During the vertical descent back to the helipad, what Nr should be maintained, and why?
options: Between 95% and 100%, so the operating engine can reach 30 second power
Above 105%, to store rotor energy for the landing
Between 100% and 104%: at or above 100% for sufficient rotor energy for the landing, and below 105% so the remaining engine produces maximum power
Exactly 100%, because 30 second power is only available at 100% Nr
items.explanation: Prior to or at the TDP: decrease collective sharply to stop the vertical climb, then descend vertically to the helipad maintaining between 100% and 104% Nr. The CAUTION explains: maintain Nr at or above 100% during the vertical descent to ensure sufficient rotor energy is available for the landing, and below 105% to ensure that the remaining engine is producing maximum power.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.6A SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD VERTICAL PROCEDURE (p.3-7)

items.question: Flying the helipad vertical-procedure land back from a high TDP in strong winds, what minimum rate of descent should the pilot ensure, and why?
options: 600 FPM, to avoid exceeding 30 seconds of 30 second OEI power
300 FPM, to limit landing gear loads at touchdown
1,000 FPM, to keep Nr above 100%
500 FPM, to avoid tail contact with the helipad
items.explanation: When the land back maneuver is flown in strong winds from a high TDP, the aircraft may require more than 30 seconds to return to the ground if the rotor is below 105%. The pilot should ensure a minimum descent rate of 600 FPM to avoid exceeding 30 seconds of 30 second OEI power. In this unusual case, it is permitted to descend at 105% Nr.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.6A SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD VERTICAL PROCEDURE (p.3-8)

items.question: An engine fails after the TDP during a ground level helipad vertical takeoff. What is the first action?
options: Decrease collective sharply and descend vertically to the helipad
Rotate to approximately 5° nose up and continue the vertical climb
Raise collective to 30 second power and hold a level attitude until Vtoss
Decrease collective to maintain Nr above 95% while rotating the aircraft to 20° below the horizon
items.explanation: After TDP: 1. Decrease collective to maintain Nr above 95% while rotating the aircraft to 20° below the horizon. 2. Rotate to approximately 5° nose above the horizon when approaching Vtoss. 3. Climb at Vtoss or above at 100% Nr. 4. Landing gear up when a positive rate of climb is established. Minimum drop down is attained by initially rounding out 5 knots below Vtoss and then accomplishing a climbing acceleration to Vtoss using 30 second OEI power.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.6A SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD VERTICAL PROCEDURE (p.3-8)

items.question: For a rejected takeoff after an engine failure during a Category B takeoff, at about what height does the RFM call for a partial flare?
options: About 20 feet
About 50 feet
About 100 feet
About 200 feet
items.explanation: If gross weight and flight path permit, a Category B takeoff and climbout may be continued. For a rejected takeoff: reduce collective pitch as necessary to maintain Nr if altitude permits, make a partial flare at about 50 feet to reduce ground speed, apply collective to cushion ground contact, neutralize cyclic and reduce collective to minimum, and apply brakes to minimize ground roll.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.7 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKEOFF — CATEGORY "B" (p.3-8A, p.3-9)

items.question: After a single engine failure during cruise, under what condition does the RFM say to consider an air restart?
options: Always, as soon as single engine airspeed is established
Only if the APU can be started as an air source
Only if the cause of the failure has been determined and corrected
Only after descending below 5,000 feet
items.explanation: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE: adjust collective to maintain desired Nr while transitioning to single engine airspeed; select two minute and then maximum continuous power when conditions permit (not two minute power until obstacle clearance is assured). Consider an air restart per ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT only if the cause of failure has been determined and corrected. If restart fails or no attempt is made, follow EMERGENCY ENGINE SHUTDOWN, and land as soon as practical.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.8 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE (p.3-9)

items.question: How does the RFM define the Category A Landing Decision Point (LDP) for a horizontal approach, and what applies if an engine fails after it?
options: 200 feet above intended landing elevation, 50 KIAS and 600 FPM rate of descent; after the LDP the approach must continue to touchdown
100 feet above intended landing elevation, 40 KIAS and 500 FPM; after the LDP a go around is still permitted
200 feet above intended landing elevation, 70 KIAS and 1,000 FPM; after the LDP the approach must continue to touchdown
50 feet above intended landing elevation, 50 KIAS and 300 FPM; after the LDP a go around is still permitted
items.explanation: A Category A LDP is defined as 200 feet above intended landing elevation, 50 KIAS and a descent rate of 600 feet per minute. If an engine failure occurs at or above the LDP, the pilot may elect to perform a go around or continue the landing. If the engine failure occurs after the LDP, the approach must continue to touchdown.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.9 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING HORIZONTAL APPROACH — CATEGORY "A" (p.3-9)

items.question: An engine fails before the LDP on a Category A horizontal approach and the pilot elects to go around. What are the initial collective and pitch targets?
options: Collective for Nr above 95%, pitch for 55 KIAS or above
Collective for 105% Nr, pitch for Vy of 80 KIAS
Collective for 100% Nr (ensuring 30 second power is activated), pitch for 70 KIAS
Collective for 104% Nr, pitch for 50 KIAS
items.explanation: Prior to or at the LDP, balked landing (go around): 1. Adjust collective to maintain 100% Nr (ensure 30 second power is activated). 2. Adjust pitch attitude to maintain 70 KIAS. 3. Landing gear up when a positive rate of climb is established. Two minute power is not selected until obstacle clearance is assured.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.9 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING HORIZONTAL APPROACH — CATEGORY "A" (p.3-9, p.3-10)

items.question: During a Category A or B single engine landing, after confirming 30 second power is armed, when is the deceleration initiated?
options: Passing 200 feet and 50 KIAS
Passing 100 feet and 70 KIAS
Passing 20 feet and 35 KIAS
Passing 50 feet and 50 KIAS
items.explanation: SINGLE ENGINE LANDING — CATEGORY "A" OR "B": 1. Confirm 30 second power is armed. 2. Initiate deceleration passing 50 feet and 50 KIAS. 3. Use collective to cushion touchdown. 4. After touchdown, neutralize cyclic and simultaneously reduce collective to minimum. 5. Apply brakes as necessary to stop within confines of the landing area.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.10 SINGLE ENGINE LANDING — CATEGORY "A" OR "B" (p.3-10)

items.question: An engine fails before the LDP on an approach to a ground level helipad and the pilot elects to go around. What are the first two actions?
options: Adjust collective to maintain 100% Nr and pitch to maintain 70 KIAS
Adjust collective to maintain Nr above 95% and pitch to obtain 55 KIAS or above
Lower collective to keep Nr above 105% and pitch to 35 KIAS
Select two minute power and pitch for Vy
items.explanation: Ground level helipad, prior to or at the LDP (go around): 1. Adjust collective to maintain Nr above 95%. 2. Adjust pitch attitude to obtain 55 KIAS or above. 3. Adjust collective to maintain 100% Nr. 4. Landing gear up when a positive rate of climb is established. Two minute power is not selected until obstacle clearance is assured. If the engine fails after the LDP, the pilot is committed to land.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.11 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING APPROACH TO A GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.3-10)

items.question: After the LDP on a single engine approach to a ground level helipad, what does the RFM require before and during the flare?
options: At least 50 KIAS and no more than 600 FPM before the flare, and flare at 20 feet
At least 35 KIAS and no more than 500 FPM before the flare, flare initiated at 50 feet and completed before descending below 20 feet
At least 55 KIAS and no more than 300 FPM before the flare, and flare completed below 10 feet
At least 35 KIAS and no more than 1,000 FPM before the flare, and flare initiated at 100 feet
items.explanation: After LDP, single engine landing: maintain at least 35 KIAS and no more than 500 FPM rate of descent prior to the flare, and initiate the flare at 50 feet to slow the rate of descent and reduce ground speed to zero. The CAUTION states that to prevent tail to ground contact, the flare should be completed prior to descending below 20 feet. Then descend vertically in a landing attitude and cushion the landing with the collective.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 1.11 SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING APPROACH TO A GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.3-10A)

items.question: Upon a dual engine failure, which way will the helicopter nose swing, and why?
options: To the right, due to the reduction in torque
To the left, due to the reduction in torque as engine power decreases
To the left, due to the tail rotor overspeeding
It will not swing; the AFCS holds heading automatically
items.explanation: Upon dual engine failure, the helicopter nose will swing to the left due to reduction in torque as the engine power decreases. Immediate collective reduction is required to maintain Nr within safe limits; full down collective should be maintained until Nr recovers to the normal operating range, and rudder pedals should be applied to maintain heading.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 2.0 DUAL-ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-10B)

items.question: What does the WARNING for a dual engine failure while hovering or on takeoff at 10 feet or less caution against?
options: Failing to move the cyclic forward while lowering the collective, which can decrease main rotor blade to tail cone clearance
Raising the collective before ground contact, which can overtorque the drivetrain
Applying wheel brakes before the collective is fully down
Holding a level attitude, which can cause a nose-low touchdown
items.explanation: The WARNING states that failure to move the cyclic forward while lowering the collective can decrease the main rotor blade to tail cone clearance and increase the possibility of striking the tail cone with a rotor blade. Actions: hold the aircraft in level attitude, increase the collective as required to cushion the landing, then after ground contact lower collective to minimum and apply wheel brakes.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 2.1 DUAL ENGINE FAILURE WHILE HOVERING OR ON TAKEOFF AT 10 FEET OR LESS (p.3-10B)

items.question: Following a dual engine failure in cruise, what rotor speed and airspeed does the procedure call for?
options: Reduce collective to maintain Nr at 100% and establish a 60 to 70 KIAS glide
Reduce collective to maintain Nr at 110% and establish a 50 to 60 KIAS glide
Reduce collective immediately to maintain Nr at 105% and establish an autorotative glide between 80 and 100 KIAS
Maintain Nr at 96% and hold 120 KIAS until the landing site is selected
items.explanation: DUAL ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE: 1. Reduce collective immediately — maintain Nr at 105%. 2. Establish autorotative glide between 80 and 100 KIAS. 3. LDG GEAR — DN. 4. Fuel and engine throttles — OFF. 5. Cabin occupants — alert. If time and altitude permit, try to restart one or both engines; if neither engine will start, perform an autorotative landing.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 2.3 DUAL ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE (p.3-11, p.3-12)

items.question: In autorotation, at what airspeeds are the minimum rate of descent and the maximum glide distance attained?
options: Minimum rate of descent (2,200 to 2,400 fpm) at 80 KIAS; maximum glide distance (0.6 nm/1000 feet) at 100 KIAS
Minimum rate of descent at 100 KIAS; maximum glide distance at 80 KIAS
Both at 85 KIAS
Minimum rate of descent at 60 KIAS; maximum glide distance at 120 KIAS
items.explanation: The minimum rate of descent of 2,200 to 2,400 fpm may be attained at 80 KIAS and 100 to 105% Nr. The maximum glide distance of 0.6 nm/1000 feet may be attained at 100 KIAS and 100 to 105% Nr.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 2.3 DUAL ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE (p.3-11)

items.question: During an autorotative landing, at what height is the flare executed, and what nose-up attitude should not be exceeded as the flare loses effectiveness and the helicopter settles?
options: At 50 feet; maximum 15° nose up
At 200 feet; maximum 5° nose up
At 100 feet; maximum 20° nose up
At 100 feet; maximum 10° nose up
items.explanation: AUTOROTATIVE LANDINGS: establish an 80 to 100 KIAS autorotative glide (recommended flare airspeed is 85 KIAS minimum), maintain Nr at 105%, gear down. At 100 feet, execute a flare to decrease airspeed, decrease sink rate and increase Nr. As the flare loses effectiveness and the helicopter starts to settle, reduce flare to a maximum 10° nose up. Prior to ground contact, increase collective to cushion landing; immediately after landing decrease collective, neutralize cyclic and apply wheel brakes.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 2.4 AUTOROTATIVE LANDINGS (p.3-12)

items.question: ENG 1 HOT START is displayed (TGT above 1000° during start). After moving the throttle to STOP, what does the procedure call for?
options: Press the ENG START button and motor the engine until TGT decreases below 250°
Turn FUEL OFF and wait until TGT decreases below 150° before any motoring
Press the ENG START button and motor the engine until TGT decreases below 540°
Discharge the fire extinguisher into the affected engine
items.explanation: The FADEC hot start prevention logic should automatically abort a normal start attempt when TGT reaches 1000°; it is not provided during emergency start procedures. For ENG HOT START (TGT greater than 1000° during start): 1. Throttle (affected engine) — STOP. 2. ENG START button — PRESS. 3. Motor engine until TGT decreases below 250°.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.1 ENGINE HOT START (p.3-13)

items.question: With a FADEC Channel B failure (FADEC 1B FAIL or FADEC 2B FAIL), which cautions for the affected engine are disabled?
options: ENG OIL HOT, FUEL BYPASS and ENG OIL PRES
ENG OIL BYPASS, ENG FUEL PRES and ENG CHIP
ENG POWER LIM and ENG RATE LIM
No cautions are disabled by a single channel failure
items.explanation: Channel B failure: loss of the affected engine oil pressure and TGT indications, ENG POWER LIM caution illuminates, and ENG OIL BYPASS, ENG FUEL PRES and ENG CHIP cautions are disabled. (Channel A failure disables ENG OIL HOT, FUEL BYPASS and ENG OIL PRES instead.) Complete loss of a single FADEC channel will not degrade engine performance; loss of both channels on one engine will cause that engine to fail. In flight: land as soon as practical. On the ground: correct prior to flight.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.2 FADEC CHANNEL FAILURE (p.3-13, p.3-14)

items.question: A FADEC 1 XENG caution (cross engine communications fault) illuminates. What does the CAUTION say about the affected engine, and what are the actions?
options: The affected engine is limited to maximum continuous power; select two minute power only below 500 feet
The affected engine will not respond to collective changes; shut it down immediately
30 second power will be armed on the affected engine; avoid high engine power settings and rapid collective movements, and land as soon as practical
Load sharing is lost; match torques manually with the throttle and continue the flight
items.explanation: FADEC CROSS ENGINE COMMUNICATIONS FAULT (FADEC 1 XENG or FADEC 2 XENG). CAUTION: 30 second power will be armed on the affected engine. Action: 1. Avoid high engine power settings and rapid collective movements. 2. Land as soon as practical.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.3 FADEC CROSS ENGINE COMMUNICATIONS FAULT (p.3-14)

items.question: In an ENGINE FIXED POWER ("fail fixed") condition, collective has been reduced to try to get a rate of descent at 80 KIAS. When does the procedure require the affected throttle to be moved to STOP in flight?
options: As soon as the torque split is noticed
When Nr increases above 106% and torque on the good engine reaches 0 before a rate of descent can be established
When Nr decreases below 100% during the collective reduction
Only once on the ground, never in flight
items.explanation: Actions: 1. Airspeed — 80 KIAS. 2. Collective — make small changes to confirm the fail fixed condition. 3. Collective — reduce until a rate of descent is obtained or Nr increases above 106%. If Nr increases above 106% and torque on the good engine reaches 0 before a rate of descent can be established: 4. Throttle (affected engine) — STOP, then 5. accomplish SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE procedure. The WARNING notes that in a fail fixed condition there is no automatic engine overspeed protection. If a descent rate can be obtained at 80 KIAS, the approach and landing may be made with the fail fixed engine on line.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.4 ENGINE FIXED POWER (p.3-15, p.3-16)

items.question: In a "fail fixed" condition you move the affected throttle to STOP, but the engine does not shut down. What does the RFM say to do?
options: Move the throttle to IDLE, which will bring the engine to idle
Press the FIRE/ARMED pushbutton to cut fuel
Cycle the FADEC channel circuit breakers
Shut the engine down by moving the affected fuel switch to OFF
items.explanation: In a fail fixed condition, moving the affected throttle to IDLE will not cause the engine to go to idle. If moving the throttle to STOP does not cause the engine to shut down, shut down the engine by moving the affected fuel switch to OFF.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec III: 3.4 ENGINE FIXED POWER (p.3-16)
